problem:
The equation below describes all the points on the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ},$ where $P(-3,5,0)$ and $Q(0,-3,2).$

$$
r(t)=[\begin{aligned}a \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -8 \\ b\end{aligned}],\,t\in [c,1]
$$

What is the value of $a+b+c?$

activity_context.topic_title: The Vector Equation of a Line

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Line Segment
examples.problem: Using $\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j},\mathbf{k}$ notation, find a parametrization of the line segment $\overline{PQ},$ where $P(-4,1,2)$ and $Q(-2,5,-1).$
examples.worked_solution:
We need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =(-2\,i+5\,j-k)-(-4\,i+j+2\,k) \\  & =2\,i+4\,j-3\,k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{p} + t \mathbf{v} 
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
\mathbf{r} = (-4 \, \mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} + 2\,\mathbf{k}) + t (2 \, \mathbf{i} + 4 \, \mathbf{j} - 3 \, \mathbf{k})
$$

and the parametrization of the line segment $\overline{PQ}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =(-4\,i+j+2\,k)+t(2\,i+4\,j-3\,k) \\  & =(2t-4)\,i+(4t+1)\,j+(2-3t)\,k,\,t\in [0,1].\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Consider the straight line that passes through $P(3,1,1)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨-1,0,2⟩.$ Find all the possible points $A$ on that line such that $AP=\sqrt{5}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the vector equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =⟨3,1,1⟩+t⟨-1,0,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Since $A$ lies on the line, we know that there must be a real number $t$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OA} & =⟨3,1,1⟩+t⟨-1,0,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PA} & =\overset{\to }{OA}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =(⟨3,1,1⟩+t⟨-1,0,2⟩)-⟨3,1,1⟩ \\  & =t\,⟨-1,0,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-t,\,0,\,2t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the fact that $PA=\sqrt{5},$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}AP & =\sqrt{5} \\ |\overset{\to }{PA}| & =\sqrt{5} \\ |⟨-t,\,0,\,2t⟩| & =\sqrt{5} \\ \sqrt{(-t)^{2}+(0)^{2}+(2t)^{2}} & =\sqrt{5} \\ \sqrt{{t}^{2}+0+4{t}^{2}} & =\sqrt{5} \\ \sqrt{5{t}^{2}} & =\sqrt{5} \\ \pm \sqrt{5}t & =\sqrt{5} \\ t & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, putting the values $t=\pm 1$ into the equation for the line, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{O{A}_{1}}=⟨3,1,1⟩+⟨-1,0,2⟩=⟨2,1,3⟩, \\  & \overset{\to }{O{A}_{2}}=⟨3,1,1⟩-⟨-1,0,2⟩=⟨4,1,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the points are ${A}_{1}(2,1,3)$ and ${A}_{2}(4,1,-1).$
